issue: Does the federal ban on firearm possession by convicted felons, 18 U.S.C. § 922(g)(1), violate the Second Amendment, at least as applied to a person with a nonviolent prior conviction, after New York State Rifle & Pistol Ass'n v. Bruen?

sides.position: Section 922(g)(1) and felon-in-possession convictions do not violate the Second Amendment, because Congress acted within the historical tradition in enacting the felon prohibition.
cases: United States v. Jackson, 69 F.4th 495 (8th Cir. 2023)

sides.position: Section 922(g)(1) is unconstitutional as applied to a prospective gun owner whose only prior conviction was a state conviction for making a false statement to obtain federal food stamps.
cases: Range v. Att'y Gen., 69 F.4th 96 (3d Cir. 2023) (en banc)

quote: A circuit split exists regarding the constitutionality of felon-in-possession convictions.
cite: United States v. Marlon Johnson, 95 F.4th 404 (6th Cir. 2024)
